text:
max.ross: Hi folks — I moved back to Canada (BC) from the US on 2025-09-20 but my last two paystubs still show US federal/state withholding and no Canadian CPP/EI. I also noticed my country in ADP still says US. Can someone help get me onto Canadian payroll going forward and handle any retro corrections? I filed an HR relocation form but wanted to flag here.

nina-peopleops: Thanks for the heads up, Max. Can you confirm the date you became a Canadian tax resident and upload your proof of address + work authorization to the HR portal? We need that to start Canadian onboarding. Also ping @luke-payroll so payroll can advise on retro adjustments.

max.ross: Uploaded the lease and PR card scan to Portal > Documents > Payroll. Residency date is 2025-09-20. I also updated my address in Gusto but not sure if that flows to ADP.

luke-payroll: Thanks Max. We usually need: 1) proof of move, 2) completed Canadian payroll forms (TD1-ON/TL2 where applicable), and 3) confirmation of tax residency change. Once we have docs we request the vendor to: a) stop US payroll withholding from the pay period covering 2025-09-21 onward, b) register/run Canadian payroll for post-move periods, and c) propose retro allocations for YTD wages.

emily-hr: FYI — benefits implications: provincial health deductions and RRSP enrolment changes may apply; I'll follow up if anything needs manual change.

max.ross: Will this affect my 2025 W-2 or require a W-2c? Also will I get a T4 from Canadian payroll for 2025?

luke-payroll: Good questions. Possible outcomes: if US withholding occurred for pay after your Canadian residency date, payroll may issue a W-2c to amend US boxes, and the Canadian vendor will issue a T4 for Canadian-source wages. Sometimes vendors reallocate wages between jurisdictions instead of issuing both docs, but we'll confirm. Timeline typically 2-6 weeks after vendor receives documents.

tax-bot: Ticket PR-4789 created for Max Ross payroll relocation. Status: awaiting vendor confirmation and completed Canadian TD1.

nina-peopleops: Max — please fill out the attached TD1-BC and federal TD1 in the HR portal under "Payroll Forms" (or upload signed PDFs). If you prefer, we can DM you a checklist.

max.ross: Done — TD1s submitted. Thanks all. Anything I should expect for filing 2025 taxes across both countries?

luke-payroll: Likely you'll file part-year returns: US (to report US-source wages and claim refunds for any overwithholding) and Canada (to report Canadian-source wages). We can share our cross-border tax guide and connect you with our tax partner for residency and treaty questions. We'll note potential duplicate withholding and advise on how vendor will correct.

emily-hr: I'll also check benefits enrolment dates and sync with payroll so deductions align once Canadian payroll starts.

max.ross: Appreciate it — keep me posted here or on PR-4789. :thumbsup:
